chunks: And Dāwūd ibn Sirḥān narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:
Regarding a man who carried goods on his head and struck a person, who then died, or broke something of his, he said: “He is exempt from liability.”

key_terms.فَمَاتَ: the resulting death of the person struck
key_terms.مَأْمُونٌ: deemed free from liability or indemnity in this case

ai.seo_question: Is a person liable if he accidentally harms someone while carrying goods on his head?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about accidental harm caused while carrying goods. It indicates that in this described circumstance, the person is treated as maʾmūn, meaning not held liable for the resulting death or damage.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5219 - Dawud ibn Sirhan narrated from Abu Abdullah (as)

regarding a man who was carrying goods on his head and accidentally struck a person, causing death or breaking something.
Imam (as) said: "He is not held liable (ma'mun)."
